title: Text Elements & Formatting Tags
summary: Master essential HTML tags for typography, including headings, paragraphs, ordered and unordered lists, and emphasis.
body:
# Text Elements & Formatting Tags Text is the primary medium for conveying information on the internet. Browsers provide native semantic elements that give written text structure, hierarchy, and meaning for human readers and assistive technology like screen readers. ## Headings and Paragraphs HTML offers six levels of section headings, from `

` through `

`, and deeper subdivisions use `

` through `

`. Never skip heading levels just to alter font size—use CSS for styling. Paragraphs are created using `

` tags. Browsers automatically insert margin before and after paragraphs to maintain comfortable vertical spacing. ## Lists for Organized Information When grouping related items, HTML provides two primary list types: - Unordered lists (`

    `): Use bullet points for items where order does not matter (like ingredients or navigation menus). - Ordered lists (`
      `): Use numbers for sequential instructions or ranked items. Each item inside both list types must be wrapped in a list item (`
    1. `) element. ```html

      Daily Morning Routine

      Follow these essential steps every morning:

      1. Hydrate with a glass of water.
      2. Review your top three tasks for the day.
      3. Take a ten-minute walk outside.
      ``` ## Adding Emphasis When certain words need special emphasis, use semantic inline tags: - ``: Indicates strong importance or urgency; browsers render this bold by default. - ``: Indicates conversational stress emphasis; browsers render this italicized by default.
